overall_rationale: Across the blinded pairs, the stronger frames consistently used the available viewport for a legible focal diagram, visible prompt choices, and distinct numbered teaching anchors. The weaker frames most often rendered the same conceptual system as a faint overview with low-contrast or microscopic labels; compact viewports also exposed label collisions and edge clipping when prose labels replaced concise callouts. Both sides were often close on wide desktop compositions, but short landscape and mobile layouts produced decisive differences in teaching usability and accessibility-visible legibility.
